A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Easi3R research and contain 15 readable pages, including Appendices A–D. Their text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Easi3R segmentation, camera-pose and reconstruction results in Section 4, plus ablations and additional evaluations in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports Easi3R's own experimental results in Section 4 and the appendices, including quantitative comparisons, ablations and qualitative reconstructions.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same attention aggregation, clustering-based segmentation, second-pass attention reweighting and optional flow-guided global alignment.

E1.justification: Coverage remains DAVIS, DyCheck, ADT, TUM-dynamics, Sintel, BONN, KITTI and static ScanNet, with the same segmentation, pose, depth and reconstruction tasks. The additional appendix evaluations already appear in v2.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including DUSt3R, MonST3R, DAS3R, CUT3R and the broader appendix comparisons in Tables 8–10. The newly cited reference [76] is not introduced as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain the same SAM2 and optical-flow settings, sequence downsampling, alignment procedures and metrics. The alternative evaluation protocols described in Appendix D are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 6, 7 and 11 retain the same attention-map, clustering, decoder-reweighting, flow-mask and hyperparameter ablations. The static-scene and failure-case analyses in Appendices C–D also match.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The temporal attention means and standard deviations belong to the unchanged method, rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 1–11 and the qualitative findings match. For example, Easi3Rmonst3r retains DAVIS-16 with-SAM2 JM=70.7 in Table 1, and Easi3Rdust3r retains DyCheck ATE=0.021 in Table 3.

T1.justification: Equations 1–16 and their mathematical definitions and reasoning are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free attention adaptation, motion disentanglement, reconstruction and performance relative to existing methods.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and interpretations remain unchanged. Appendix C retains the limitation that inaccurate backbone depth predictions and boundary floaters can persist despite improved global reconstruction.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same default window size, 64 clusters, Otsu thresholding, runtime, image resolution and RTX 4090 hardware. Project-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zhao et al., Pseudo-generalized dynamic view synthesis from a video (2023), as reference [76]. Section 2 attaches it to the existing statement that static-scene reconstruction methods degrade on dynamic videos; broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: The supplementary introduction replaces references to Appendix A–D with Sec. A–D, and the arXiv version/date marker is updated. There are no substantial paragraph rewrites or section reorganizations.

P2.justification: Small typesetting and spacing changes occur, including local reflow from the shorter supplementary introduction and the added bibliography entry. Figures 1–13 and Tables 1–11 retain their content, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: The added citation provides a small attribution benefit, while cross-reference and typesetting edits have little effect on readability. The method, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
